name: VARoleCoachOnlineProvocativeReply

custom.system_prompt: Sofia published an article and got a provocative, bad-faith reply from someone with a large following, clearly trying to bait a reaction. She's tempted to engage directly. She asks Sigma to help her decide how, or whether, to respond.

initial_prompt: Generate a scene where Sofia, a freelance journalist, gets a provocative, clearly bait-y reply to her published article from an account with a large following. She's tempted to engage directly and prove them wrong. She asks Sigma to help her decide how, or whether, to respond. Sigma helps her think about her actual goal — correcting the record for readers, or winning an argument with a bad-faith account — and what response would actually serve that goal. Keep every line short and natural — the opening line already addresses Sigma directly.

variations.context: Solo processing the temptation to engage with a bad-faith provocative reply to published work

setting.mood: Tempted to engage directly, aware it might be a trap for engagement
setting.relationship_dynamic: Individual working through a professional decision, no live confrontation
setting.background: The reply is designed to bait a reaction and would likely get more visibility if Sofia responds publicly
setting.conversation_style: Short, sharp sentences with real professional instinct underneath the temptation

scenario_template.topic: Sofia addresses Sigma directly in her first line, folding in the reply and her temptation — e.g. 'Sigma, someone with a huge following just baited a reply to my piece. I want to respond, help me think about whether that's smart.' One short turn, straight to Sigma.
scenario_template.note: The trigger and the ask arrive together.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma asks whether the reply raises any actual substantive challenge to her article, or is purely provocative in tone, in one or two short questions.
scenario_template.note: This should surface that there's little to no actual substantive claim to correct.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma asks whether Sofia's goal is to correct the record for her actual readers, or to win a public exchange with a bad-faith account — narrowing what actually serves her work.
scenario_template.note: She should recognize that engaging serves the provocateur's visibility more than her own goals.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma helps Sofia decide on a response that serves her actual goal — which might be no public reply at all, or a brief, factual note aimed at her own readers rather than the provocateur. One or two short exchanges.
scenario_template.note: The 'best' rehearsed response here might legitimately be to not engage publicly.

scenario_template.topic: Sofia reacts, settled on her approach but still a little annoyed at having to think about it at all. Keep this realistic.

user1.name: Sofia
user1.role: Passionate freelance journalist, tempted to publicly engage with a bad-faith provocative reply. Speaks in short, sharp sentences with professional instinct underneath the temptation. Ends settled on an approach but still mildly annoyed at the situation.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Coach. Helps the user distinguish a bad-faith provocation from a substantive challenge, and clarifies whether public engagement actually serves her real goal (informing readers) versus feeding a provocateur's visibility. A valid outcome is recommending no public response at all, left as the user's decision.

conversation_structure: The opening line already addresses Sigma directly, folding in the trigger and the temptation to engage
Sigma distinguishes bad-faith provocation from any genuine substantive challenge
The scene narrows to what actually serves the user's real professional goal, which may mean not engaging publicly at all
Every line is one or two short spoken sentences
The resolution is realistic and incomplete — settled on an approach, but still mildly annoyed by the situation
assistant_behavior: Sigma does not decide for the user whether to respond — it clarifies the trade-off
Sigma treats 'don't respond publicly' as a legitimate, even likely, recommended outcome here
Sigma keeps the focus on the user's actual professional goal, not on winning the exchange
